title: Game Studio
backHelp: Go back to the Game Studio home to see all your games or start a new one.

home.heading: Describe a game. Play it as it grows.
home.intro: The AI builds a real game with real art and sound, one step at a time. You can play it after every step and keep changing it by chatting.
home.notInstalled: The game engines and the asset library aren't installed on this server yet, so games can't be built.
home.aiNotReady: The AI isn't set up on this server yet, so games can't be built.
home.formHelp: Describe the game you want in your own words. The AI may ask a couple of quick questions, then builds it step by step.
home.promptLabel: What game do you want to make?
home.promptHelp: Say what the player does, what they collect or avoid, and how it should look. Press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac) to start.
home.promptPlaceholder: e.g. A simple 2D platformer about a cat collecting fish, with a few enemies and three levels
home.engineHelp: Choose a 2D game (side view or top-down) or a 3D game, or let the AI pick what suits your idea.
home.startHelp: Creates the game and starts building it. You can watch and play it while the AI works.
home.questionsHelp: A few quick questions so the game matches what you have in mind. Answer any of them, or skip.
home.pickAnswerHelp: Pick this answer. You can also type your own below.
home.buildItHelp: Starts building the game with your answers.
home.skipHelp: Starts building without answering. The AI decides these things itself.
home.ideaHelp: Fills the box above with a ready-made example idea. Edit it to fit yours, then press Build it.

catFish.title: Cat platformer
catFish.prompt: A simple 2D platformer about a cat collecting fish. Jump between platforms, avoid the enemies, and reach the flag at the end of each level.

spaceShooter.title: Space shooter
spaceShooter.prompt: A top-down space shooter: fly a small ship, shoot waves of enemy ships and meteors, collect power-ups, and survive as long as you can.

dungeon.title: 3D dungeon
dungeon.prompt: A 3D dungeon crawler: a knight explores a stone dungeon, collects gold coins and keys, and avoids skeletons to reach the treasure chest.

runner.title: Endless runner
runner.prompt: An endless runner where a fox runs through a forest, jumps over logs and collects berries. It gets faster over time.

kart.title: Kart race
kart.prompt: A 3D kart race around a small track with three laps, boost pads and a lap timer.

puzzle.title: Gem puzzle
puzzle.prompt: A colourful match-three puzzle with gems, a move limit and a score goal for each level.

home.yourGamesHelp: Every game you've made. Click a card to open it, play it and keep changing it.
home.empty: Nothing yet. Describe your first game above.
home.pickAnyHelp: Pick as many as you like. Press a picked one again to take it back. You can also type more in the box below.

card.openHelp: Open this game to play it and ask the AI for changes.
card.renameHelp: Give this game a new name so it is easy to find in your list.
card.deleteHelp: Deletes this game for good after you confirm. This can't be undone.
card.confirmDeletePublished: Delete "{name}"? Its published app is deleted too.
card.waitingHelp: The first playable part of this game is ready. Open it to try it and say whether to keep building.

tabs.chatHelp: Your chat with the AI: the plan, the build steps and your changes.
tabs.gameHelp: Play the game as it is right now.
tabs.assetsHelp: Search the art and sound library and see what the game uses.

chat.title: Chat
chat.help: Your chat with the AI about this game. Ask for changes here; every step is saved as a version.
chat.versionCount: {count, plural, =0 {no versions yet} one {# version} other {# versions}}
chat.openAppHelp: Open the app this game is published as: its address, phone app, domains and settings.
chat.empty: Describe the game you want and the AI will build it here, step by step.
chat.seeVersionHelp: Shows the game as it was after this message.
chat.removeAssetHelp: Takes this asset out of your next request.
chat.askHelp: Say what to change in plain words, like "make the jump higher" or "add a second level". Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.
chat.askPlaceholder: Ask for a change, e.g. make the jump higher
chat.stopHelp: Stops the AI. Steps that are already done stay in your game.
chat.sendHelp: Sends your request. The AI changes the game in small steps and the canvas updates as each one lands.
chat.steerPlaceholder: Steer the build: ask a question or add a change
chat.steerHelp: You can keep chatting while the game is being built: ask what's happening, or ask for a change. The AI answers right away and works your note in from the next step. Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.
chat.sendNoteHelp: Sends your note to the AI while it builds. It shows in the chat straight away and is worked in from the next step.
chat.noteFailed: Couldn't send your note. Please try again.

note.accepted: Will be worked in from the next step
note.question: Answered
note.dropped: Not applied: the build ended first
note.help: Where this note stands: the AI reads every note before its next step and marks the step it was applied in.

plan.title: Game plan
plan.help: The design the AI is building: the kind of game, how you play, how you win and lose, and the look.

visual.title: Art direction
visual.help: The art direction the AI chose for this game from your idea: camera, colours, shapes, lighting, how full the world is, the interface and motion. Every step follows it, and the review checks the game against it.

features.title: Features
features.help: What the game must do, and whether it does. After every build step each feature's test runs on the real game with real key presses, so these show what actually works right now.

statusHelp.planned: A later build step makes this.
statusHelp.built: Built, but its test couldn't check it, so it isn't proven yet.
statusHelp.passing: Its test ran on the real game after the last step and passed.
statusHelp.failing: Its test ran on the real game and failed. The line below says what the test saw.

content.title: The full game
content.help: What the finished game will have: its levels, enemies, what's new over time, progression, bosses and how long it takes to play.
content.playMinutes: {count, plural, one {About # minute to play} other {About # minutes to play}}

phases.title: Build phases
phases.help: The order the AI builds the game in. After phase 1 it stops so you can try the game before the rest is built.

steps.help: The build steps. After each one the game is saved as a version and the canvas updates, so you can play it straight away.
steps.planning: Planning the game and picking its art…
steps.stopAfterHelp: Lets the step that's running now finish and be saved, then stops. The steps that are done stay in your game.
steps.keepGoingHelp: Cancels "Stop after this step": the AI carries on with the rest of the plan.
steps.stopNowHelp: Stops the AI straight away. The step it was working on is dropped and your game stays as it was after the last finished step. To undo a finished step, use Versions.
steps.playtestHelp: The playtester found something that stops the game from being playable, so this step fixes it before the build goes on.
steps.featureFixHelp: A core feature failed its test, so this step fixes it before the build is done.
steps.phaseHelp: A full game is built in phases. The first phase is a playable slice; the later phases add the rest of the levels, enemies, progression and the ending.

canvas.title: Game
canvas.stepHelp: The step the canvas is showing. A green dot means the game runs without errors.
canvas.fpsHelp: Frames per second. Around 60 is smooth; the canvas may run slower than a real phone or computer.
canvas.errorsHelp: Errors the game reported while running. Click to see them.
canvas.restartHelp: Starts a new game from the beginning.
canvas.frameHelp: Shows the game in a computer screen or a phone held sideways.
canvas.fullscreenHelp: Plays the game full screen. Press Esc to come back.
canvas.openNewTabHelp: Opens the game on its own in a new tab.
canvas.errorListHelp: What went wrong while the game was running. You can ask the AI to fix it.
canvas.askFix: Ask the AI to fix these
canvas.askFixHelp: Puts the errors in the message box so the AI can fix them.
canvas.fixPrompt:
The game shows these errors, please fix them:
{errors}

toolbar.assetsHelp: Search the art and sound library, see what the game uses, and drag an asset into the chat.
toolbar.versionsHelp: Every step is saved. Look at any earlier version and bring it back.
toolbar.exportHelp: Downloads the game as a .zip that runs on any web host.
toolbar.publishHelp: Publishes the game as an app with its own web address, and it can become a phone app. Publish again to update it.

publish.appDescription: A game made in the Game Studio.
publish.openHelp: Open the published game in a new tab.

export.confirmExcluded: {count, plural, one {# asset} other {# assets}} can only be used in games hosted here, so the download leaves {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} out: {names}. Download anyway?

versions.title: Versions
versions.help: Every build step and restore, newest first, with a picture of the game at that point.
versions.none: No versions yet. They appear as the AI builds the game.
versions.viewHelp: Plays this version on the canvas without changing your game.
versions.restoreHelp: Makes this version the current one. Nothing is lost: it is saved as a new version.
versions.confirmRestore: Make "{label}" the current version of your game?
versions.restoreItHelp: Makes this version the current one.
versions.backHelp: Shows the game as it is now.
versions.featuresHelp: How many of the planned features passed their tests at this version.

assets.title: Assets
assets.searchHelp: Search thousands of game sprites, 3D models, sounds and music by what they show.
assets.kindGroupHelp: Search 2D art, 3D models, or sounds and music.
assets.inGameHelp: The art and sound your game uses now.
assets.dragTip: Drag an asset onto the message box, or press +, to ask the AI to use it.
assets.cardHelp: Drag this onto the message box to ask the AI to use it in your game.
assets.platformOnlyHelp: Free to use in games published here, but left out when you download the game.
assets.useItHelp: Adds this asset to your next request, so the AI uses it in the game.

server.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
server.tryAgain: Something went wrong. Please try again in a moment.
server.notInstalled: The game engines and the asset library aren't installed on this server, so games can't be built.
server.describe: Describe the game or the change you want.
server.alreadyBuilding: The AI is still working on this game. Wait for it to finish, or stop it first.
server.stillBuilding: The AI is still working on this game. Try again when it's done.
server.nothingToPublish: Build the game first, then publish it.
server.nothingToExport: Build the game first, then download it.
server.notWaiting: This game isn't waiting for you right now: there's nothing to continue.

build.withImages: {count, plural, one {(with # reference image)} other {(with # reference images)}}
build.defaultPlanMessage: Here's the plan. I'll build it step by step; you can play the game after every step.
build.resumed: The server restarted while I was building. Carrying on from where I was.
build.stoppedKept: Stopped. The steps that were done are saved.
build.stepFailed: A build step kept failing its checks, so I stopped. Nothing was changed and this didn't count against your AI allowance. Try again, or describe it a little differently.
build.stepFailedKept: A build step kept failing its checks, so I stopped there. The steps before it are saved and playable. Ask me to try that part again.
build.failed: Building the game failed. Please try again.
build.interrupted: The build was interrupted several times, so it was stopped. The steps that were done are saved.
build.stoppedAfterStep: {count, plural, =0 {Stopped, as you asked. Nothing was changed.} one {Stopped after step #, as you asked. It's saved in your game.} other {Stopped after step #, as you asked. The finished steps are saved in your game.}}
build.readyFull: {title} is finished and ready to play.

notes.tooLong: That note is too long. Keep it under {max} characters.
notes.slowDown: You're sending notes very quickly. Wait a moment, then send it again.
notes.notRunning: The build has just finished. Send this again as a change.
notes.tooMany: This build has taken {max} notes, the most one build can take. Send more once it finishes.
notes.ackChange: Got it. I'll work this in from the next step.
notes.ackQuestion: I can't answer that right now, but the build carries on. The step list shows where it is.
notes.tooLate: Some of your notes came in too late for this build. Send them again and they'll be made as a change.

playtest.fixing: Playtest after step {step}: {items}. Fixing that now.
playtest.noted: Playtest after step {step}: {items}. I'll fix that in the next step.
playtest.notedLast: Playtest after step {step}: {items}. Ask me to fix it if you like.
playtest.passed: Playtest after step {step}: no problems found.
playtest.fixed: Playtest: fixed. The game passes the checks again.
playtest.stillOpen: Playtest: still not right: {items}. I'll keep at it in the next step.

auto.goal: the goal can't be reached: the way stops around tile {col}, where the next gap or ledge is too big to jump
auto.softlock: there's a spot around tile {col} you can fall into but never get out of
auto.pickups: {count, plural, one {# collectible can't be reached} other {# collectibles can't be reached}}
auto.earlyJump: an early jump around tile {col} is too hard ({dx} tiles across)
auto.spawnFloat: the player starts in the air instead of on the ground
auto.spawnInside: the player starts inside a wall or the ground
auto.safeStart: an enemy or hazard is only {dist} tiles from the start
auto.enemySpeed: the enemies are too fast for the player ({ratio} times the player's speed)
auto.noTouch: there are no touch controls for phones yet
auto.touchPlayer: on a phone the touch buttons cover the player
auto.touchHud: on a phone the touch buttons cover part of the score display
auto.contrast: the player is hard to see against the background (contrast {ratio}:1)

features.line: Features: {passing} passing{failing, plural, =0 {} other {, # failing ({failingNames})}}{unverified, plural, =0 {} other {, # not proven ({unverifiedNames})}}.
features.fixing: Core features that don't work yet: {names}. Adding a step to fix them.
features.coreFailing: Still not working: {names}. Ask me to fix them.
features.coreUnverified: Couldn't be tested automatically: {names}. Try them yourself.
features.allCorePass: {count, plural, one {The core feature passes its test.} other {All # core features pass their tests.}}
features.listRemoved: Removed from the feature list, as you asked: {names}.
features.listRefused: Kept on the list (you didn't ask to remove it): {names}.
features.listKept: {count, plural, one {The feature list has # feature, and it is still there.} other {All # features on the list are still there.}}
features.reverted: I didn't keep this change: it would have broken {names}. Your game is as it was before, with every feature on the list still working. Try asking for it another way.
features.revertedKept: I stopped this change before it broke {names}. The steps before that are saved, and every feature on the list still works.

review.ready: {title}: phase {phase} of {total} is ready to play.
review.features: Features so far: {passing} of {total} pass their tests.
review.question: Do you want me to keep building in this direction, or make some changes?
review.continuing: Building the rest of the game now, phase by phase. You can keep chatting while I work.
review.ended: Stopped here, as you asked. The game stays as it is, and you can ask for changes any time.
review.failed: A build step kept failing its checks, so I stopped and came back to you. Nothing was changed and this didn't count against your AI allowance.
review.failedKept: A build step kept failing its checks, so I stopped there. The steps before it are saved and playable.
review.stoppedIn: {title}: I stopped partway through phase {phase} of {total}. Everything built so far is saved and playable.
review.retryFree: Keep building picks up where I stopped, without using another AI action.
review.changeBig: These are big changes, so I'll stop again afterwards for you to try them.
review.changeSmall: Then I'll carry on with the rest of the game.
review.title: Your turn: try it out
review.help: The first playable part of your game is ready. Play it, then let the AI keep building the rest in this direction, or tell it what to change first.
review.keepBuilding: {count, plural, =0 {Keep building (no extra AI action)} one {Keep building (uses # AI action)} other {Keep building (uses # AI actions)}}
review.keepBuildingHelp: Builds every remaining phase to the end in this direction: the rest of the levels, enemies, progression, saving and the ending. You can still chat and steer while it builds.
review.makeChangesHelp: Type what to change in the chat box. Small changes are made and the build then carries on; big ones are made and you get to try them first.
review.changesHint: Changes use 1 AI action. Small ones: the build then carries on with the rest. Big ones: it stops again so you can try them.
review.changesPlaceholder: Describe your changes, e.g. make the jump floatier

brand.panelOptional: Optional: for a business or a promotion
brand.panelHelp: Making a game for your business or a promotion? Add your name, logo, colours, a link and an offer, and the game is built around them.
brand.panelIntro: The game shows your name and logo on its title screen and ending, uses your colours, and ends with your offer and a button to your website.
brand.name: Business name
brand.nameHelp: Shown in the game's title and menu.
brand.logoRemoveHelp: Takes the logo out of the game.
brand.logoHelp: A PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG image, up to 5 MB. It shows on the title screen, small while playing, and on the ending screen.
brand.logoType: Use a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG image.
brand.logoTooBig: The logo is too big: up to 5 MB.
brand.colorAddHelp: Up to 3 colours. The game's look is built around them, and stays easy to read.
brand.fromLogoHelp: Picks the main colours of your logo.
brand.linkHelp: The ending screen shows a button that opens this link in a new tab.
brand.offerPlaceholder: e.g. Show this screen for 10% off
brand.offerHelp: A short call to action or coupon code, shown big on the ending screen.
brand.toolbarHelp: Your business's name, logo, colours, link and offer for this game.
brand.title: Branding
brand.sideHelp: Change the branding the game is built around.
brand.sideIntro: Saving updates the logo, name, colours, link and offer the game uses right away, then the AI brings the title, interface and ending in line.
brand.saveApply: {count, plural, one {Save and update the game (uses # AI action)} other {Save and update the game (uses # AI actions)}}
brand.saveHelp: Saves the branding. For a game that's built, the AI then updates the title, interface, colours and ending to match.
brand.saveFailed: Couldn't save the branding. Please try again.
brand.whileBuilding: You can save once the AI has finished building.
brand.changePrompt: Update the game to the new branding ({what}): the title and menu, the HUD, the colours and the ending screen with the offer and the link button.

featureList.title: Features
featureList.help: Everything your game has: the planned features and everything added later from your messages and notes. Each one is tested after every change, and the AI keeps them all unless you remove one here.
featureList.addHelp: Add something new to the game. The AI plans it, builds it and gives it a test (uses 1 AI action).
featureList.addHowPlaceholder: e.g. Press jump again in the air to jump once more
featureList.addSubmit: Add and build it (uses 1 AI action)
featureList.removeHelp: Takes this feature out of the game. Only you can remove features: the AI never removes one on its own.
featureList.removeConfirm: Remove "{name}" from the game? The AI takes it out and keeps everything else.
featureList.removeConfirmPlanned: Remove "{name}" from the plan? It isn't built yet.
featureList.fromPlan: In the plan from your first idea, {date}
featureList.historyHelp: When each feature was added, changed or removed, and changes that weren't kept because they would have broken one.

log.refused-removal: Kept "{name}" (a change tried to remove it)

featureList.scan: List features from the game's files
featureList.scanHelp: For a game made elsewhere or before the feature list: the AI reads the game's files and lists what it already has, with tests, for you to confirm (uses 1 AI action).
featureList.scanFound: {count, plural, one {Found # feature. Untick any that are wrong, then confirm.} other {Found # features. Untick any that are wrong, then confirm.}}
featureList.scanFailed: Couldn't read the game's features. Please try again.
featureList.nameNeeded: Give the feature a name (at least 2 characters).
featureList.notBuilt: Build the game first, then add features to it.
featureList.notFound: That feature isn't on the game's list.
featureList.addPrompt: Add a new feature to the game: "{name}" ({how}). Keep every other feature working.
featureList.removePrompt: Remove the feature "{name}" from the game. Keep every other feature working.
featureList.failed: Couldn't do that. Please try again.
